_doc: The fleet registry — the ONE place that knows which repos and tracks exist.
Repos are declared here. Tracks are DISCOVERED by scanning each repo's tracks_glob, so this
file can never go stale on a track that was added or renamed. Per-track annotations below are
only for things a track.config.json cannot know about itself (its owning repo's build command,
its place in the four-kind taxonomy, migration status).

airoso itself is the first repo (engine_repo: true): it IS the engine, so the pin and shadowing rules (S1-S4) do not apply to it, while S5-S8 do. Its tracks_glob names only the tracks whose source of truth has moved here; a retired repo lists the same directory under moved_out, so the track is discovered once, at airoso.
Read it with: python3 -m fleet.cli tracks

absorbed_from.remote: deleted 2026-10-31 (docs/ORG-CONSOLIDATION.md): its full history is inside doooom-fast/k10-track-agents
absorbed_from.status: history cloned in full and PUBLISHED (private); tags identical in both remotes; consumers not yet re-pointed (fleet/MIGRATION.md M2)

kinds._doc: Kevin's four track types. Orthogonal to `archetype` (the construction philosophy in scripts/config.py ARCHETYPES) but they should agree — see fleet/STANDARDS.md S6.
kinds.fictional_street_circuit: A racing loop invented on top of real streets (Sand Creek Raceway). archetype: street_circuit
kinds.street_port: Real public road(s) ported as they exist, single route or whole network (Lookout Lariat, Lake Murray, SD freeway). archetype: real_road
kinds.circuit_port: A real purpose-built facility, extant or historical (IMI, High Plains, Second Creek, PPIR). archetype: race_circuit
kinds.rally_stage: A real point-to-point special stage, gravel or the tarmac fiction (Rally Colorado). archetype: real_road TODAY (kerb/runoff off, which is right); a dedicated `rally_stage` archetype is PROPOSED, not implemented — see fleet/STANDARDS.md S6

repos.name: airoso
repos._remote_doc: No GitHub remote is configured: `git remote -v` lists only `engine` (the local k10-track-agents clone whose history airoso adopted, docs/V3-PLAN.md Phase 1).
repos.role: THE one repo (V3): the engine, the gates, the doctrine and the ledger, plus every track as its source of truth moves here
repos._tracks_glob_doc: Only the tracks that have MOVED here. The other tracks/ dirs are Phase-1 imports whose fleet entry still points at their retired repo, and globbing them now would discover every Colorado track twice (S7 slug collisions). Widen this glob as each track moves, and add its dir to the old repo's moved_out in the same edit. A list since 2026-10-28: Milford is the first track born here rather than moved.

build.hold: no fleet build: fleet.cli build is the retired multi-repo control plane (docs/ONE-CHAIN.md section 2 row 11). Every track here is built by the chain, tools/ship_track.sh <track> + tracks/<track>/ship.json, on the Windows box; scripts/build.sh is the draft alone. The Lariat's chain run is owed (started 2026-11-01, ledger 0048).

repos.method: V3: engine first draft -> Claude authors in Blender (AUTH_* layers) -> gates on the built kn5 -> Kevin's drive (docs/V3-PLAN.md, fleet/REALISM.md)
repos.notes: The Lariat moved here 2026-10-11 (tracks/lookout-lariat/V3-PLAN.md P0 step 5, ledger 0048), was shelved 2026-10-12 and unshelved 2026-11-01 (Kevin: 'Start the lariat'). Its July derived data is restored, frame-free files only, in tracks/lookout-lariat/data/source-july/ (PROVENANCE.md there).

repos.method: blender-first (live operator bridge) for refinement; headless seed + export
repos.notes: Un-forked 2026-07-25 (MIGRATION M3): the 72-module shadow tree is deleted and every stage runs from .engine/. 64 of 72 were byte-identical to the engine, 8 were older, none carried anything the engine lacked. Its audit had been grepping a 'KERB' prefix against groups named '1KERB_*', so the curb-flush check reported '0 of 0' for months.

repos.notes: SD-unique code is legitimate and declared above. Anything OUTSIDE the allowlist that shadows an engine module is drift.

track_annotations._doc: Keyed by <repo>/<track-dir>. `kind` is the taxonomy; `fidelity` records how honestly the geometry is sourced; `owner_of` marks a track that supersedes a stale copy elsewhere.
